surfaces.part: oil-stained earth patch with scattered debris (rusty sheet, concrete lumps, glass shards, cable)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 64px-wide by 48-row rectangle of ground texture. Column scans show mottled earth tones with no front-edge line, eave shadow, or vertical face at the bottom. The debris clusters at rows 0-15, 17-31 and 33-47 are small details lying on the earth and are drawn from above. There is no front face of 3 or more rows, so this is a flat ground decal seen from above, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The earth is a mottled brown with about 4-5 visible lightness steps and speckled grain. It has no large flat areas (near-flat coverage 1%, against 0% for both references). Visible tones per tile are 5, above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7), so density is comparable to the grass kind. Dark edge pixels are only 2% neutral, so the debris outlines lean brown/rust and not black, which is a dark material tone and not the sticker look. Weak points: the debris pieces are small and sparse, each with only 3-4 tones, and the oil stain barely reads. The soil grain is closer to random dither than to clumped soil texture. These keep it slightly below the references, but it does not look flat or sticker-like beside them, so it passes narrowly.
